chunks: My father (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, from his father, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from al-'Is ibn al-Qasim, from Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) who said:
Whoever looks at one with a disability, or one who has been mutilated, or a person suffering from an affliction, then let him say secretly to himself without letting the person hear:
"Praise be to God who granted me wellness from what He has afflicted you with, and had He willed, He would have done the same to me"
three times, and then that affliction will never befall him.

key_terms.بلاء: Affliction, trial, calamity sent as a test from God
key_terms.عافاني: Granted me wellness/safety, spared me from affliction
key_terms.عاهة: Physical disability, bodily defect, chronic affliction
key_terms.مثل به: One who has been mutilated or disfigured

ai.seo_question: What supplication should one say when seeing a person with a disability or affliction in Islam?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) teaches a supplication of gratitude to be recited silently when encountering someone with a physical disability or affliction. The teaching emphasizes both gratitude for one's own wellbeing and sensitivity toward the afflicted person by requiring it be said privately. This was guidance given during the second century AH, addressing the social etiquette of how believers should respond to seeing suffering -- not with pity that might embarrass the person, but with private thankfulness to God and recognition that all conditions are by divine will.

en.bilal-muhammad: My father (rh) narrated to us. He said: `Ali b. Ibrahim narrated to us from his father from Safwan b. Yahya from al-`Is b. al-Qasim from Abi `Abdillah al-Sadiq (as). He said:

Whoever sees one with a disability, or one similar to that, or a suffering person, then he should say privately to himself in a way that the person would not hear: “Praise be to Allah who granted me wellness from what he is suffering from. If He willed, He would have afflicted me with this (alhamdulillahil lathi `afani mimma abtalak bih, wa law sha’a lafa`al bi thalik)” three times, then he will never be afflicted with that.
